pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Iowa journeyman electrician examination is part of the statewide licensing process through the Iowa Electrical Examining Board. The Board’s electrical examination program is administered through PSI Services LLC. Candidates must follow the current Iowa and PSI instructions for examination registration, scheduling, testing rules, and licensing steps. The Iowa journeyman electrician exam requires a passing score of 70%. The State of Iowa testing information states that passing the PSI exam with a score of 70% or higher can qualify a candidate for Iowa electrical license classifications such as Class A Master, Class A Journeyman, Residential Master, Residential Electrician, and certain Special Electrician licenses, depending on the license type and qualification pathway. Iowa journeyman candidates should prepare for an NEC-based examination that measures both electrical code knowledge and electrical theory.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Iowa electrical licensing exam program uses open-book testing for electrical exams. Candidates are expected to follow the approved reference rules issued by the testing provider and the state. Open book testing allows the use of approved references, but it still requires strong preparation and efficient code navigation. Open book does not mean the exam is easy. The National Electrical Code is a large technical reference, and candidates who are unfamiliar with its layout can lose time searching through the wrong sections. A prepared candidate should know how to identify the subject of the question, locate the correct article or table, understand the wording, and apply the rule correctly. The included National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs is designed to help candidates practice code navigation before exam day.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Iowa electrical licensing is handled through the statewide electrical licensing system under the Iowa Electrical Examining Board. Candidates applying for a new license may apply by examination, by apprentice program, or by proof of work experience, depending on the license type and qualification path. A typical Iowa journeyman electrician path includes completing qualifying supervised electrical work experience, completing an approved apprenticeship or accepted training pathway when applicable, gathering documentation, applying for the proper license classification, taking the required PSI examination if testing is required, receiving a passing score, and completing the remaining Iowa licensing requirements. Iowa recognizes Class A and Class B journeyman electrician licenses. A Class A journeyman electrician license is commonly associated with completion of an approved apprenticeship training program or another training and experience path accepted by the Board, along with meeting examination requirements.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Iowa has a statewide electrical licensing structure. The Iowa Electrical Examining Board oversees electrical licensing, and candidates must follow the requirements connected to the specific credential they are pursuing. This statewide structure helps distinguish Iowa from states where electrical licensing is handled only at the local level. Iowa recognizes different electrical license classifications, including master-level and journeyman-level credentials. A master electrician license is an advanced credential for electricians who have moved beyond entry-level and journeyman-level work. Master-level candidates are expected to understand code requirements, electrical theory, installation rules, calculations, and practical decision-making at a higher level. pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: Effective Iowa master electrician exam preparation should include code study, calculations, reference navigation, and repeated practice questions. The NEC is a large and detailed code book, and candidates need to understand how to use it as a working reference. Simply owning the code book is not enough. Candidates should practice finding answers, reading table notes, checking exceptions, and applying code language to realistic electrical scenarios. The 2026 Iowa Master Electrician Study Guide helps candidates create a more organized study routine. A strong routine may include reviewing one topic area, locating the related sections in the NEC, answering practice questions, reviewing missed answers, and returning to the code book to understand why the correct answer is correct. The 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide supports one of the most challenging parts of exam preparation.

pieces.t: Calculation questions may involve conductor ampacity, temperature correction, adjustment factors, box fill, raceway fill, service load calculations, feeder calculations, branch-circuit requirements, motor full-load current, overcurrent protection, transformer sizing, and demand factors.
